## Introduction

The following document is separated into 3 major sections, Data Cleaning, Tests and EDA (Exploratory Data Analysis). For each section, a explanation of the analysis to be done and its intent is highlighted at the beginning. This is followed by a subsection with code and output which has as embedded notes on what the code is doing. Lastly, a notes subsection for each of the major sections delves into what was surprising about the data and/or analyses. Prior to delving into these major sections, a subsection of the introduction highlights the research question for reference. A conclusion section is also included to summarize the analysis and findings. 

### Question

How does greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agrifood systems for the top 5 producing countries differ and change over the 20 year period from 2001 to 2021?

## 1 Data Cleaning

The data will be cleaned to only include relevant columns, that is those that show the country, year and amount of GHG emissions for agrifood systems produced for that year. Then the column names will be re-labeled. Also any irrelevant rows will be removed, such as World and South Asia data as these are not countries and are unrelated to the research question. Furthermore, only data between the relevant 20 year period, that is 2001 to 2021 will be kept.

### 1.1 Code & Output

```{r}
### Load Packages###
 
#install.packages("tidyverse")
#install.packages("janitor")

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(countrycode)
library(janitor)

```

```{r}
###Reading CSV File & Viewing Data###

unedited_data <-
  read_csv("../Inputs/unedited_data.csv") #Reading data from csv file stored in folder

head (unedited_data) #Viewing top 6 rows
tail (unedited_data) #Viewing bottom 6 rows
```

```{r}
###Cleaning Data to Include Only Relevant Columns###
 
cleaned_data <- 
   select(unedited_data, # Referencing the unedited data
         REF_AREA_LABEL, # Selecting column with the country names
         TIME_PERIOD, # Selecting column with the year
         OBS_VALUE) # Selecting column with the amount of GHG emissions in kilotonnes for that year

head(cleaned_data) # Viewing the top 6 rows of the selected data
```

```{r}
###Relabeling Column Names in the Cleaned Data###

cleaned_data <-
cleaned_data |>
  as_tibble() |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    Country = ref_area_label,
    Year = time_period,
    GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes = obs_value
    ) |>
  select(Country, Year, GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes)

head(cleaned_data)
```

```{r}
### Filtering the Data to Only include Country Data###

countries <- codelist |>
  select(country.name.en)

cleaned_data <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Country %in% countries$country.name.en)

cleaned_data
 
```

```{r}
### Filtering Data to only includes the years from 2001 to 2021###

cleaned_data <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Year %in% 2001:2021)

cleaned_data

```

### 1.2 Notes

The first thing that was surprising was that the data had World data and some other non-country data such as data for South Asia. When graphs for EDA was done during the weekly practices the values for these categories either skewed the graph, int he case of the world data which was the total values for all the countries or made it difficult to figure out the top producing countries, int he case of South Asia which ranked relatively high but consisted of data from numerous counties in South Asia. As such only country data based on the country list was include for EDA in this assignment.

## 2 Tests

Then, the class of each column will be checked to ensure that values are of the right class. Further tests using "validator" will be done to ensure that the data in each column adheres to certain rules. A csv file of the cleaned data will be created.

### 2.1 Code & Output

```{r}
### Load Packages###

#install.packages("validate")

library(validate)

```

```{r}
### Test to check the class of all columns###

class(cleaned_data$Country) 
class(cleaned_data$Year)
class(cleaned_data$GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes)

```

```{r}
### Checking that all the country names in the data matches in the country names in the list###

if (all(unique(countries) %in% cleaned_data$Country)) {
  "The cleaned countries match the expected countries"
} else {
  "Not all of the countries match the expected countries"
}
  
```

```{r}
### Test to check which countries in the list are not in the cleaned data###
setdiff(
  unique(countries$country.name.en),
  unique(cleaned_data$Country)
)
```

```{r}
###Test to check if data in columns adheres to certain rules###

rules <- validator(
  is.numeric(Year), #Checking if the column is numeric
  is.character(Country), #Checking if the column a character
  is.numeric(GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes), #Checking if the column is numeric
  Year %in% 2001:2021, # Checking if the years between 2001:2021
  Country %in% countries$country.name.en #Checking that all the countries names are in the country list
)

out <-
  confront(cleaned_data, rules)
summary(out) 

```

```{r}
###Create CSV File of Cleaned Data###

write.csv(cleaned_data, "cleaned_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

### 2.2 Notes
In the test that checks whether the country names in the cleaned data aligns with the countries in the list it was found that, not all the countries in the cleaned data aligned with the country in the list. This was surprising, however the other test using validate confirmed that all the countries in the clean data were on the country list but not all the countries in the list was in the cleaned data.The other test listed the countries in the on the list that were not in the cleaned data. Surprisingly there were many popular countries that were excluded and a quick skim of the unedited data showed that as a result of variation in names, for example "Venezuela" in the list vs "Venezuela, RB" in the edited data, many countries were excluded in the data cleaning process. However, at this stage it was decided that these countries would be left out instead of further cleaning the data to include them. This decision was made as none of the countries excluded are likely candidates for being in the top 5 countries producing GHG emission for agrifood systems. Thefefore, their irrelevance to the research question at this point in this means that the cleaned data was not adjusted to include these countries. However, in future, that is in the data story data cleaning may follow another process to ensure countries with data are not left out.


## 3 Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) 

After using popular functions to look at the data, three exploratory graphs will be created to help better understand the data. First, a line graph of the GHG Emission for all the countries. This will broadly demonstrate which countries are the top GHG emissions for agri-food systems. Once the top 5 countries are identified, a graph of the average amount GHG emissions for agrifoods systems over the 20 year period for the top 5 producing countries will be plotted, this will illustrate which country produces the overall highest amount of GHG emissions for agrifood systems. Lastly, a bar chart showing the net difference in GHG emissions in agrifood systems for the top 5 producing countries between 2001 and 2021 will be plot. This will illustrate how much countries increased or decreased their overall GHG emissions for agrifood systems over 20 year period.

### 3.1 Code & Output

```{r}
### Load Packages###

#install.packages("readr")
#install.packages("ggrepel")

library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(ggrepel)

```

```{r}
### Reading Cleaned Data from the CSV file###

cleaned_data <-
  read_csv("../Inputs/cleaned_data.csv")

cleaned_data

```

```{r}
###Using popular functions to get a look at the data###

head(cleaned_data)

tail(cleaned_data)

cleaned_data |>
  slice_sample(n = 5)

glimpse(cleaned_data) 

summary(cleaned_data)
```

```{r}
###Plotting a line graph###
    
label_data <- cleaned_data |>
  group_by(Country) |>
  slice_max(Year, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  slice_max(GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes, n = 5)

cleaned_data |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Year,
    y = GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes,
    group = Country
  )) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = label_data,
    aes(
      x = Year,
      y = GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes,
      label = Country
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Greenhouse Gas Emissions by Country Over Time",
    x = "Year",
    y = "GHG Emissions (Kilotonnes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
### Bar Graph of Mean Agrifood Systems GHG Emissions for Top 5 Emitting Countries Between 2001 and 2021###

top5 <- c("China", "Brazil", "India", "United States", "Indonesia")

mean_top5 <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Country %in% top5) |>
  group_by(Country) |>
  summarise(Mean_Emissions = mean(GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(mean_top5, aes(x = reorder(Country, Mean_Emissions), y = Mean_Emissions, fill = Country)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Agrifood Systems GHG Emissions for Top 5 Emitting Countries Between 2001 and 2021",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean Emissions (Kilotonnes)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 
```

```{r}
### Bar Chart Showing the Net Difference in GHG Emissions in Agrifood Systems for the Top 5 Producing Countries between 2001 and 2021###

change_top5 <- cleaned_data |>
  filter(Country %in% top5, Year %in% c(2001, 2021)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year,
    values_from = GHG_Emissions_Kilotonnes,
    names_prefix = "y"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Change = y2021 - y2001,
    Direction = ifelse(Change >= 0, "Increase", "Decrease")
  )

ggplot(change_top5, aes(x = reorder(Country, Change), y = Change, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Increase" = "firebrick", "Decrease" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in GHG Emissions Between 2001 and 2021 for Top 5 Emitting Countries",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Change in Emissions (Kilotonnes)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 3.2 Notes

Also surprising was that once the line graph of all the countries was plotted it was very easy to identify which countries were the to 5 producers of GHG emissions for agrifood systems. They were quite apparent from the line graph and so further analysis like creating wide data from the cleaned data and calculating the average GHG emissions for agrifoods systems for each country to figure out which countries had a highest values over the 20 year period, a step that was in the original plan, was no longer necessary.

Additionally, in regards to the line graph the final version that is shown only includes the country labels for the 5 top countries, previous versions of the graph included all the country labels however, they were difficult to read. After a few trials editing the code and being unsuccessful in finding a was to clearly show all the country labels, the decision was made to only include the labels for the top 5 countries producing the highest GHG emissions for agrifood systems. This decision was made given that the research question is only concerned with the top 5 producing countries and so it make sense to do this in this context, however should others want to use this graph late outside of this context it may not be as useful to them.
